resources.string: We need a special permission to continue. Use ADB to run the following command (one line):
adb shell \"pm grant io.github.jkmungara.comatoseplus android.permission.WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS; pm grant io.github.jkmungara.comatoseplus android.permission.DUMP\"
Applied and verified. The system is using these values.
Applied. Grant the DUMP permission to confirm it took effect.
Applied, but the system is not using the new values. %1$s
No profile applied yet. The system defaults are in use.
Last applied: %1$s (not verified). Tap to copy the command that enables verification.
Last applied: %1$s, but the system is not using it.
Android (API %1$d) does not let apps change Doze settings directly. Run this on a computer with ADB, or grant root access and tap the profile again:\n\n%2$s
Permission was revoked. Grant it again to continue.
Use the device\'s default idle settings
Additional savings with slightly less timely notifications
A state of deep sleep where background processes and checks are delayed
Save as much power as possible with large sacrifices to background work
Is the phone really entering deep idle?
Profile the rest of the day
Auto-revert profiles you pick by hand

Changes happen at the exact time on most devices. If Android blocks exact alarms they can be late. A profile you pick by hand stays until the next scheduled change, or until the auto-revert time you choose here. Force-stopping the app clears the alarms until you open it again.
No finished sessions yet. A session is a stretch of at least an hour on one profile while not charging. Use a profile overnight and check back.
\nDrain includes anything you did with the phone during a session, so compare overnight sessions.
This check reads the system\'s Doze history, which needs the DUMP permission. Run this on a computer with ADB, then try again:\n\n%1$s
Could not read the Doze history.
Right now: deep idle state %1$s, light idle state %2$s.\n\n
No Doze history yet. Leave the phone idle with the screen off and check again.
Over the last %1$s of history, the phone spent %2$s in deep idle (%3$d%%), in %4$d stretches with %5$d maintenance windows.
Most of that time was spent in deep idle.
Little deep idle. Charging, movement, or apps that stay active can keep the phone out of deep idle.
